Seborrheic keratosis is common in adults and may appear pinkish, especially when inflamed or early; however, it’s typically more verrucous or waxy and less likely to be truly pink or rapidly evolving—still highly plausible. Cherry angioma is benign, common, and characteristically bright red to pink, but usually smaller (<3 mm), asymptomatic, and does not typically enlarge over weeks—so moderately plausible but less so than BCC or seborrheic keratosis. Squamous cell carcinoma in situ (Bowen disease) can present as a pink, scaly, slowly enlarging patch or plaque; while less commonly nodular or bump-like, its presence on sun-damaged skin and potential for evolution warrants inclusion, albeit with lower confidence due to atypical morphology for this diagnosis."}
